_doc: Footprint SLA budgets for the ai-brain-starter hook fleet. HARD axes (block merge): per-event/per-tool substrate cold-start fan-out + default-on daemon count + DEAD once:true flags (a once flag is ignored in settings.json -> a 'once' hook re-fires every event; move it to SessionStart). Advisory: per-hook timing + per-message injected tokens (axis D, injected_tokens_per_message ceiling) are reported by --measure --execute, gated in CI only via --selftest controls. See docs/adr/0004-footprint-sla-gate.md.

_budget_rationale.fanout_per_event.SessionStart: 18 -> 19: activating hooks/sessionstart-hook-snapshot-guard.py (MYC-1031 / MYC-3880), which warns when a SessionStart hook DISAPPEARS from settings.json. Same never-wired history as the PreToolUse entries below: it shipped with MYC-1031 and sat on check-hook-activation.py's UNCLASSIFIED_BASELINE its entire life, so the drift protection it appears to give did not exist. Worse, when MYC-3880 finally read it, its identity function collapsed all 19 Windows hook commands into one shared identity, so even a wired copy could not have reported a drop unless the whole fleet vanished at once -- dormant AND broken, each hiding the other. Cost is honest about where it lands, and this is the cheap end of the SessionStart fleet: one interpreter spawn, two small JSON reads (settings.json + its own snapshot), a regex over ~20 short command strings, and a set difference. No filesystem walk, no subprocess, no network, no git -- scripts/audit-sessionstart-boundedness.py --all confirms it is not in the corpus-walk freeze class that governs this event. It writes only on baseline or addition; the warning path deliberately does not write, so a real drop stays reported until reconciled. Bought against drift its sibling structurally cannot see: surface-deployed-hooks-behind.py catches settings.json falling BEHIND hooks.json, and nothing caught a hook being pruned OUT of settings.json by a linter, a manual edit, or a parallel session. Note this raise consumes the last of the SessionStart headroom rather than adding to it -- the event measured 18/18 before this hook, so the next SessionStart addition should optimize the fan-out (Stage 2: dispatcher / async) rather than raise again.
_budget_rationale.fanout_per_tool.PreToolUse.Bash: 8 -> 9: activating block-skip-prefix-in-vault-write.py, the `__SKIP` privacy guard. Cost is honest about where it lands: every call pays one interpreter spawn, a JSON parse of the payload, and a short-circuiting scan of the PATH string against 7 folder regexes. A path outside a life-record surface returns without ever reading the content. Only a write to a journal / coaching / processing-note / panel path pays the content scan for the token. Bash is not a secondary path here: skills/daily-journal/SKILL.md instructs writing journal files with `cat > ... <<EOF` rather than the Write tool, so this matcher is where the primary journal write is actually caught. It additionally pays a shlex split of the command segments to honor the inline `SKIP_PREFIX_BYPASS=1` prefix, and only a command that matches a life-record path AND contains a redirect marker pays the token scan. Bought against content the user explicitly marked as not-for-persistence reaching a file. That is unrecoverable once written: it is in the file, in git history, and in every index built over the vault. A warning that is ignored still writes, so this blocks. Prior rationale, still in force: 7 -> 8: activating block-claude-mcp-inline-secret.py (MYC-3560), which blocks `claude mcp add ... --env NAME=<secret>`. Shipped after the 2026-05-19 github-mcp PAT leak but never registered anywhere, so the protection it appears to give did not exist. Cost is honest about where it lands: every Bash call pays one interpreter spawn, a JSON parse of the payload, and one regex search for `claude mcp add`; only a command that actually matches pays the further `--env`/`-e` secret-pattern scan. Prior rationale, still in force: 6 -> 7: activating block-git-mutation-mid-operation.py, the in-flight git-operation gate (incident 2026-07-28). Cost is honest about where it lands: non-git Bash calls pay one interpreter spawn plus a substring test and return; a git call with a MUTATING verb pays one `git rev-parse --git-dir` subprocess, and reads HEAD as a plain file rather than spending a second subprocess on it. Reads, `git tag`, `git branch` and the --abort/--continue resolution verbs never reach the subprocess path. Bought against a measured 22-hour stalled rebase in which ~22 commits landed on a detached HEAD and six commits from four sessions fell off main — the previous entry's CONCURRENT-SESSION-HEAD-DRIFT class, in the case a liveness lock structurally cannot see. Prior rationale, still in force: 5 -> 6 activated check-cd-outside-worktree.py, the worktree HEAD-isolation gate that shipped unregistered (present on disk, dormant in behavior); a pure in-process string match on the payload cwd, no git, no I/O, returning immediately unless the session is worktree-rooted.
_budget_rationale.fanout_per_tool.PreToolUse.Write/Edit/Mu: 10 -> 11: activating block-mcp-config-inline-secret.py (MYC-3560), which blocks a Write/Edit/MultiEdit to an MCP config file (~/.claude.json, **/.mcp.json, .claude/settings*.json) whose new content carries a secret-shaped value. Same never-wired history as the Bash entry above (written after the 2026-05-19 + 2026-05-23 PAT leaks, referenced nowhere). Intentional: the hook checks the write's basename against a 4-name fixed set before any content scan, so the common case (almost every write is not one of those 4 filenames) costs one interpreter spawn, a JSON parse, and a basename compare; the secret-pattern regex over the new content runs ONLY for an actual MCP-config-shaped path. Prior rationale, still in force: 9 -> 10: activating validate-handoff-frontmatter.py, which shipped with templates/rules/handoff-files.md documenting it as enforcement but was never registered, so the rule described a guard that did nothing on every install (issue #375, same ARTIFACT-WITHOUT-ACTIVATION class as the Bash entry above). Intentional: the hook gates on file extension before any I/O, so a non-markdown write (the common case) costs one interpreter spawn and a suffix compare; the directory walk that finds the vault root runs ONLY for a markdown file that is already a handoff missing consumes_when, which is the rare denial path.
